To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hierarchical, multi-level model of whole-body insulin sensitivity can be used to simulate the effects of different insulin signaling defects on glucose homeostasis.

a hierarchical and modular model of glucose homestasis, coupled with molecular specifications of the cellular insulin signaling cascade, is able to reproduce the dynamics of glucose homeostatic regulation in normal and diabetic conditions.

a multi-level model of whole-body metabolism, coupled with the cellular level specification of the insulin signaling, can represent the dynamics of glucose homeostatic regulation in the normal condition and in the context of type 2 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an integrative and comprehensive computational model that can be used to study the pathophysiologic mechanisms involved in the regulation of glucose metabolism in health and disease.

the design of an integrated and modular model that can serve to investigate the complex dynamics of glucose metabolism and to provide an effective tool to study and understand the molecular mechanisms of type 2 diabetes.

the construction of a comprehensive and structured model of whole-body and cellular glucose homeostasis that could be used as an in silico platform for testing the efficacy of novel pharmacological interventions in type 2 diabetes, or as an in silicio experimental environment to study the effects of environmental factors on glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is an ideal tool for the simulation of the glucose metabolism, and it can be applied in a wide range of experimental conditions, from normal physiology to pathological conditions.
the proposed model architecture represents a valuable tool for the simulation of glucose homeostatic mechanisms in normal and pathologic states.
the multi-level closed-loop modeling approach provides a promising framework for the description of complex systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multi-level closed-loop approach can be a useful tool for the description of complex biological systems and for the design of new therapeutic strategies.

a modular, hierarchical, and closed-loop model of glucose metabolism, as the one proposed in this study, can provide a useful tool for the simulation of glucose dynamics in normal and pathologic conditions.

this model could serve as a useful platform to test the effects of novel therapeutic strategies in a virtual environment, and to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of multi-level and closed loop modeling is a promising approach for the dynamic modeling of complex biological processes.

a comprehensive and structured modeling approach is a prerequisite to the design of a computational model that can provide a fair description of a complex system such as whole-body glucose homeastasis.
multi-level models can be designed to provide a seamless dynamic description, from cellular to systemic scale, of the core determinations of glucose homeostatic processes.
